classification.difficultyReason: Several linked decisions using the demonstrated definitions or procedures. The four-element power set requires all sixteen subsets without order duplicates.

content.prompt:
Given a set $X$, its $\mathit{power\ set}$, $\mathcal P(X)$, is the set containing all subsets of $X$. Write down $\mathcal P(X)$ for
$$X=\{a,b,c,d\}.$$

answer.worked:
List subsets with zero, one, two, three and four elements, counting each subset once:
$$\begin{aligned}\mathcal P(X)=\{&\varnothing,\\&\{a\},\{b\},\{c\},\{d\},\\&\{a,b\},\{a,c\},\{a,d\},\\&\{b,c\},\{b,d\},\{c,d\},\\&\{a,b,c\},\{a,b,d\},\\&\{a,c,d\},\{b,c,d\},\\&\{a,b,c,d\}\}.\end{aligned}$$
The count is $1+4+6+4+1=16$.
